_status: PROPOSED content (new in v2). Fills the gap exposed by Testrun-v1: no rule defined how a human NPC combatant is built, so the model improvised a trapper profile ("Level 2, HP maybe ~60 ... let's just make him HP 70"). Everything here is derived from existing canon; only default Levels, free-point emphasis and concrete gear values inside the Content #9 F-rank reference ranges are new choices and should be confirmed by the author.
_derivation: Lore #1: most humans receive a Base Class around adulthood -> an adult human NPC is a core-stat character with a Base Class.
Lore #3: most people remain F/E -> default Levels 1-3 (F-rank).
Content #0 + Core #3: Human baseline 5/5/5/5/5/5, class favored +1/+1 at Level 1 and on each later Level, +5 free Stat Points per later Level.
Core #2: MaxHP = 50 + Level*5 + VIT*5, MaxSTA 100, Init = AGI + floor(PER/2), Base DEF/MDEF = floor(VIT/4)/floor(WIL/4).
Content #9: F-rank gear references (Martial Weapon ATK 4-10, Light Armor DEF 2-4 / MDEF 2-5, ...).

Basic Attack: the Base Class Basic Attack (Content #1-#5). If the NPC's weapon does not fit that attack (e.g. a Ranger fighting with a hand-axe), the engine uses the Basic Attack whose weapon family matches (weapon_family_basic below) — PROPOSED rule.
free_point_rule: Per Level gained after 1: distribute 5 free points in priority order 2/2/1 over the first three stats of 'priority'.

templates.label: Adventurer (by Base Class)
templates.skills_rule: first two Offensive/Defensive entries of the class skill pool

temperaments.aggressive: closes in and attacks; retreats only at <=15% HP if sapient; beasts fight on
temperaments.cautious: attacks when it can reach; a melee-only NPC shot from range takes cover or closes in; retreats at <=35% HP
temperaments.skittish: flees once threatened or hurt; attacks only when cornered (ENGAGED with no retreat)
temperaments.defensive: holds position, attacks only targets that are ENGAGED, otherwise keeps cover
